text: Why did AT&T tell Baran his design would not work?
choices: It was genuinely impractical with 1964 technology, and it implied the network they had perfected was the wrong shape
It required more copper than existed
explanation: Both halves matter. The design was ahead of the available technology, and accepting it would have required admitting that eighty years of circuit-switching investment pointed in the wrong direction. Institutional resistance and genuine technical objection were entangled.
